entry.name: mc.sfplay~
entry.description: Use the mc.sfplay~ object to play audio files from disk. Supported formats include AIFF, WAVE, MP3, OGG, FLAC, M4A, CAF, WF64, WAVE64, and Raw Data.

arguments.name: sflist-object-name
arguments.description: If the first argument is a, it names anthat theobject will use for playing cues. If no symbol argument is given,plays its own internally defined cues.

arguments.name: number-of-output-channels
arguments.description: Sets the number of channels to output as one multi-channel signal. The maximum number of channels is 64. The default is 1. If the audio file being played has more output channels than theobject, higher-numbered channels will not be played. If the audio file has fewer channels than theobject, those channels not being used will be zeroed.

arguments.name: buffer-size
arguments.description: An additional optional argument can be used to specify the disk buffer size in samples. In general, we recommend using the default buffer size unless you are experiencing dropouts during playback.The default disk buffer size is 483840 for instances with up to 8 channels, and 80640 times the number of channels for instances with more than 8 channels.Disk buffer sizes will be rounded to the nearest multiples of 20160. If this argument has a value of 0, the default disk buffer size will be used.

arguments.name: position-outlet-flag
arguments.digest: Create an outlet that reports positioning information
arguments.description: An additional optional argument can be used to create outlets to the mc.sfplay~ object which display positioning information. Specifying a final argument ofcreates a single outlet to the left of the rightmost "bang on finish or halt" outlet which outputs a signal value which corresponds to the current playback position in milliseconds.Like all MSP audio signals, this playback position is a 32-bit single precision floating-point signal. If greater precision is desired, specifying a final argument of 2 creates a second outlet which outputs a second 32-bit single precision floating-point signal containing the single precision roundoff error. Together these signals provide near double precision floating-point accuracy. (Note: after several minutes a single precision floating-point value is no longer sample accurate) Using the two signals together with objects such as the unsupported Max/ MSP high resolution signal processing objects like, one may perform sample-accurate calculations based on file position

arguments.name: object-reference-name
arguments.digest: Name to identify the object and its contents
arguments.description: If the last argument is a symbol, it specifies a name by which other objects can refer to theobject to access its contents.

attributes.name: slurtime
attributes.digest: Slur time
attributes.description: Set the time it takes for the correction to reach the full correction amount. Typically, notes are a bit unstable at the beginning, because the attack phase of a sound has a higher amount of noise, and because singers gradually adjust their tuning after the onset of the note. The slur time makes the pitch correction sound natural because it models this effect. Higher values will yield a slower adaptation time and it will take longer for the correction to produce the corrected pitch. However, longer slur times will also preserve vibrato better.

messages.name: (drag)
messages.digest: Drag a file from the File Browser to load it
messages.description: When an audio file is dragged from the Max File Browser to anobject, the file will be loaded.

messages.name: anything
messages.digest: Play a numbered cue
messages.description: In left inlet: If the name of anobject is sent to, followed by a number, the numbered cue from theis played if it exists.

messages.name: clear
messages.digest: Clear all defined cues
messages.description: In left inlet: The wordwith no arguments clears all defined cues. After amessage is received, only the numberwill play anything (assuming there's an open file). The wordfollowed by one or more cue numbers removes them from theobject's cue list.requires the DSP chain to be off.

messages.name: dictionary
messages.digest: Define complex time stretching
messages.description: Use a dictionary to define more complex time stretching. Define a point in time (sourcetime) and define where this point should be transformed to (desttime). For example, the dictionary below will

messages.name: embed
messages.digest: Save all defined cues and the name of the current file with the patcher
messages.description: In left inlet: The message, followed by any non-zero integer, causesto save all of its defined cues and the name of the current open file when the patcher file is saved. The messagekeepsfrom saving this information when the patcher is saved. By default, the current file name and the cue information is not saved inwhen the patcher is saved. If anobject is saved with stored cues, they will all be preloaded when the patcher containing the object is loaded.

messages.name: fclose
messages.digest: Close a file and remove all cues
messages.description: In left inlet: The word, followed by the name of an open file, closes the file and removes all cues associated with it. The wordby itself closes the current file.

messages.name: float
messages.digest: Define the playback rate of an audio file
messages.description: In right inlet: Defines the playback rate of an audio file. A value of 1.0 plays the audio file at normal speed. A playback rate of -1 plays the audio file backwards at normal speed. A playback rate of 2 plays the audio file at twice the normal speed. A playback rate of .5 plays the audio file at half the normal speed. The playback rate cannot be changed when playback is off.To initiate starting from a cue point with a negative speed, bidirectional cues must be used.

messages.name: int
messages.digest: Start/stop playback of a file or cue
messages.description: In left inlet: If a file has been opened with themessage,begins playback (of the most recently opened file), andstops playback. Numbers greater than 1 trigger cues that have been defined with themessage, or that were defined based on the saved state of theobject. When the file is played, the audio data in the file is sent out the signal outlets according to the number of channels the object has. When the cue is completed oris stopped with a, ais sent out the right outlet. If the object is currently assigned to anobject (using themessage or with a typed-in argument), anwill trigger cues stored in theobject rather than inside the. To resetto use its own cues, send it themessage with no arguments.

messages.name: list
messages.digest: Define a set of cues for playback]
messages.description: In left inlet: Gives a set of cues forto play, one after the other. The maximum number of cues in a list is 128. Cue numbers (set using themessage) can be any integer greater than or equal to 2. If a cue number in a list has not been defined, it is skipped and the next cue, if any, is tried. If the object is currently assigned to anobject, a list uses cues stored in theobject. Otherwise, cues stored inside theobject are used.

messages.name: loopone
messages.digest: Enable looping for a specified cue
messages.description: In left inlet: The word, followed by a cue-number, will set only the cue specified to loop.

messages.name: modout
messages.digest: Enable modulo output for multichannel audio files
messages.description: In left inlet: The word, followed by 1, turns on modulo output. If the number of channels in a audio file is less than the number of channels for theobject, theobject will reduplicate the audio file's channels across all of thechannels (rather than outputting zero) if modulo output is enabled. For example, a mono audio file loaded into anobject with two channels will be played in both channels if modulo output is enabled. Similarly a stereo audio file will be played on anobject with four outlets with the left channel played on channels 1 and 3, while the right will be played on channels 2 and 4. The messagedisables this feature.

messages.name: offset
messages.digest: Specify a sample start offset in bytes
messages.description: In left inlet: The word, followed by a number, specifies the sample start offset in bytes. The default value is 0. This value useful for aligning samples and avoiding playback of header information.

messages.name: open
messages.digest: Open an audio file for playback
messages.description: In left inlet: followed by the name of an AIFF, WAVE, MP3, OGG, FLAC, M4A, CAF, WF64, WAVE64, or Raw format audio file or CD-audio track, opens the file for playback and makes it the current file. The word, followed by a filename, opens the file if it exists in Max's search path. Without a filename,brings up a standard open file dialog allowing you to choose a file. When a file is opened, its beginning is read into memory, and until another file is opened, you can play the file from the beginning by sendingthe message. When themessage is received, the previous current file, if any, remains open and can be referred to by name when defining a cue with themessage. If any cues were defined that used the previous current file, they are still valid even if the file is no longer current.

messages.name: openraw
messages.digest: Open any type of file for playback
messages.description: In left inlet: Themessage functions exactly like, but allows you to open any type of file for playback and make it the current file. Themessage assumes that the file being opened is a 16-bit stereo file sampled at a rate of 44100 Hz, and assumes that there is no header information to ignore (i.e., an offset of 0). The file types can be explicitly specified using the,,, andmessages.

messages.name: pause
messages.digest: Pause at the current playback position
messages.description: In left inlet: Themessage causes the audio file playback to pause at its current playback position. Playback can be restarted with themessage.

messages.name: preload
messages.digest: Define a cue
messages.description: In left inlet: Defines a cue - an integer greater than or equal to 2 - to refer to a specific region of a file. When that cue number is subsequently received,plays that region of that file. Cue number 1 is always the beginning of the current file - the file last opened with themessage - and cannot be modified with themessage.There are a number of forms for themessage. The wordis followed by an obligatory cue number between 2 and 32767. If the cue number is followed by a filename of a file in Max's search path, or a full file pathname, that cue number will play the specified file. Note that a file need not have been explicitly opened with themessage in order to be used in a cue. If no filename is specified, the currently open file is used.After the optional filename, an optional start time in milliseconds can be specified. If no start time is specified, the beginning of the file is used as the cue start point. After the start time, an end time in milliseconds can be specified. If no end time is specified, or the end time is, the cue will play to the end of the file. If the end time is less than the start time, the cue is defined but will not play. Eventually it may be possible to define cues that play in reverse.After the start and/or end time arguments, a optional directional buffer flag is used to enable reverse playback of stored cues. Setting this flag to 1 enables reverse cue playback. The default setting is(bidirectional buffering off).A final optional argument is used to set the playback speed. A float value sets theobject's playback speed relative to the object's global playback speed -- set set by either themessage or theobject's right inlet. The default value is.Each cue that is defined requires approximately 40K of memory perchannel at the default buffer size (40320), with bidirectional buffering turned off. With bidirectional buffering turned on, the amount of memory per cue is doubled.Themessage is always deferred to low priority. The,, andmessages are not. If you have problems with these messages arriving before you want them to in overdrive mode (i.e., before you've preloaded the most recent cue), use theobject.
messages.argPattern: cue-number:int, filename:symbol, start-time:number, end-time:number, directional-flag:int, playback-speed:float

messages.name: preloadn
messages.digest: Define a cue using a normalized start and end time values
messages.description: Themessage works in precisely the same manner as themessage, but normalized values in the range 0. - 1.0 are to specify start and end times for the cue.
messages.argPattern: cue-number:int, filename:symbol, start-time:float, end-time:float, directional-flag:int, playback-speed:float

messages.name: print
messages.digest: Report information about state and currently defined cues
messages.description: In left inlet: Prints information about the state of the object, plus a list of all the currently defined cues.

messages.name: resume
messages.digest: Resume playback from current position
messages.description: In left inlet: If playback was paused, playback resumes from the paused point in the file.

messages.name: samptype
messages.digest: Specify a sample type for an audio file's data
messages.description: In left inlet: The word, followed by a symbol, specifies the sample type to use when interpreting the audio file's sample data (thus overriding the audio file's actual sample type). This is sometimes called "header munging." When reading files in response to themessage, the assumed sample type is 16-bit integer. Modifications usingmake no changes to the file on disk.The following types of sample data are supported:: 8-bit integer: 16-bit integer: 24-bit integer: 32-bit integer: 32-bit floating-point: 64-bit floating-point: 8-bit "mu"-law encoding: 8-bit a-law encoding

messages.name: seek
messages.digest: Move to a specified position in the current file and begin playing
messages.description: In left inlet: The word, followed by a start time in milliseconds, moves to the specified position in the current file and begins playing. After the start time, an optional end time can be specified, which will set a point for playback to stop. Themessage is intended to allow you to preview and adjust the start and end points of a cue.NOTE: Themessage is always deferred to low priority. If you have problems with these messages arriving before you want them to in overdrive mode (i.e. before you've finished seeking to a new location), then use theobject.

messages.name: set
messages.digest: Play all cues stored in anobject
messages.description: In left inlet: The message, followed by a name of anobject, will causeto play cues stored in thewhen it receives anor. The messagewith no arguments resetsto use its own internally defined cues when receiving anor.

messages.name: signal
messages.digest: Trigger a stored cue with sample accuracy
messages.description: In left inlet: An input signal may be used for the sample-accurate triggering of prestored cues. When a signal value is received in the left inlet, the integer portion of the signal value is monitored. When the integer portion of the input signal changes to a value equal to the index of a prestored cue, that cue is triggered. Negative values are ignored.

messages.name: srate
messages.digest: Set the sampling rate for an audio file
messages.description: In left inlet: The word, followed by a number, specifies the sampling rate (Hertz) at which to interpret the audio file's sample data (thus overriding the audio file's actual sampling rate). This is sometimes called "header munging." When reading files in response to the openraw message, the assumed sampling rate is 44,100 Hz. Modifications usingmake no changes to the file on disk.

messages.name: srcchans
messages.digest: Set the number of channels for an audio file
messages.description: In left inlet: The word, followed by a number, specifies the number of channels in which to interpret the audio file's sample data (thus overriding the audio file's actual number of channels). This is sometimes called "header munging." When reading files in response to themessage, the assumed number of channels is 2. Modifications usingmake no changes to the file on disk.

inlets.digest: open Opens File, int Plays Cue, 0 Stops
